clue.text: A flower or two among things on table ?

parts.note: butter is one of the things you put on a breakfast table
a cup is another item set on a table

explanation.surface: A riddle about spotting a flower, or a pair of them, among the items laid on a table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or two' looks like a count of flowers, but it says the answer splits into two everyday table items set side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: This common yellow meadow plant of the genus Ranunculus is a familiar wild bloom.

clue.text: Cereal makes money in West — what about East?

parts.note: a buck is a dollar, money in the American West

indicators.note: the word what goes round the letter for East

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grain earns cash out West, and what of the East?
explanation.definitionFit: This grain-like seed crop is used for flour and porridge.

clue.text: French city attracting holiday-makers ?

explanation.surface: A French city that draws in tourists.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire city of that name; and trips and excursions are what pull in tourists.

clue.text: Ends ' cutting down expenses,'including new term

indicators.note: the shortened expenses word holds the rearranged letters inside

parts.note: exes is a cut-down slang form of the word expenses

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters of term

explanation.surface: Boundaries reached by trimming costs, with a new term added in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exes' is informal British shorthand for expenses; 'cutting down' says the word is a shortened form, not that costs are being reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer limits or furthest points of anything are its extremes.

clue.text: Shell mounted corps quickly

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means the letters climb, so they are read upwards

parts.note: RAC is the Royal Armoured Corps
apace means quickly

explanation.surface: Cavalry regiment shells out at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Armoured Corps (RAC) is a British Army corps of tanks; mounted also fits its former cavalry.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard upper shell of a tortoise or crab is called its carapace.

clue.text: Where 'lines intersect or diverge

parts.note: geometry places where lines cross, and railway switches where tracks split

explanation.surface: A question about where lines meet or split apart.
explanation.walkthrough: In geometry lines intersect at these, and on a railway the track 'lines' diverge at them (British railway switches are called points).
explanation.definitionFit: Geometric locations and railway switches share this one name.

clue.text: Sea point state

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the open sea
E, east, is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: A terse list of geography words: a sea, a point, a state.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a US state in New England, on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Scholars hasten to the old club

parts.note: MAs are holders of a Master of Arts degree, scholars
hie is an old word meaning hasten

explanation.surface: Learned people hurry off to an old society.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf iron of former days, roughly a modern five-iron.

clue.text: Letters from Taormina to a lover

indicators.note: the letters of the place name and a are taken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Love letters sent from a Sicilian resort to a sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: Taormina is a Sicilian resort; 'to' is the link, and the letter a ends the answer after the rearranged place name.
explanation.definitionFit: A female beloved or mistress is an inamorata, from Italian.

clue.text: Passage in book ?

parts.note: a doorway or way in, and an item written in a register or dictionary

explanation.surface: A section of text from a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' looks like a stretch of text, but it is a way in, and a record made in a book has the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A way in is an entrance, and an item recorded in a ledger or dictionary has the same name.

clue.text: Anti the census-taker

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to the official who counts the population.
explanation.definitionFit: As a prefix or adjective it means opposing, against; as a noun it is one who counts heads, as a census enumerator does.

clue.text: A second pressing.?

explanation.surface: A one-off ironing job, perhaps, or a quick press of a button.
explanation.definitionFit: A moment or split second is an instant, and in older usage an instant need is an urgent, pressing one.

clue.text: Scraps used to be 'seen by half the team

parts.note: was is the past tense of be, so used to be gives was

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word team is its first two letters

explanation.surface: Leftovers that half the side once noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' is a link before 'team'; 'half' takes the first two of team's four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraps and leftovers are rubbish, refuse thrown away.

clue.text: Heritage is cut on being put in wages

indicators.note: the pieces for cut and on are placed inside the word for wages

parts.note: pay is another word for wages
to trim is to cut

explanation.surface: Someone's inheritance is reduced once it gets paid into their salary.
explanation.definitionFit: An inheritance handed down from one's father or ancestors is one's heritage.

clue.text: Hill gives Newman's address? 7

explanation.surface: A hill tells us where a man called Newman lives.
explanation.walkthrough: John Henry Newman was a cardinal, and a cardinal is addressed as 'Your Eminence'; 'address' is a form of address, not a street. The stray 7 in the clue as held is an OCR artefact, absent from the scan.
explanation.definitionFit: A rise of ground is an eminence; it is also the honorific title used when speaking to a cardinal such as Newman.

clue.text: He doesn't know a song Muir composed

indicators.note: the letters are composed, set out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A man unfamiliar with a tune written by someone named Muir.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignorant person, someone who lacks knowledge, is an ignoramus.

clue.text: Prize tree.?

explanation.surface: A tree that won an award.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear the palm is to win a prize, the palm frond being an ancient emblem of victory; it is also a tropical tree.

clue.text: Lighter entertainment as& a matter of course

parts.note: a match is something for lighting a fire
a play is a theatrical entertainment

explanation.surface: Lighthearted fun taken as routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A matter of course' sounds like routine, but it is a golf course: match play is a golf format scored by holes won.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf format decided hole by hole is a thing played on a course.

clue.text: Rather a little thaw, perhaps

parts.note: some means a little

indicators.note: perhaps hints that thaw may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A mild melt, more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhat and rather both mean to a moderate degree.

clue.text: Dangers end climb over cascades

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters climb, so they read upwards

parts.note: a tip is the end of something
falls are waterfalls, cascades

explanation.surface: The hazards of finishing a climb by tumbling down waterfalls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is the link: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second; 'climb' makes 'end' read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidden hazards or traps are pitfalls.

clue.text: Mind some old coins?

parts.note: some stands for a number, here ten
d was the abbreviation for the old British penny, so ten d is tenpence in pre-decimal money

explanation.surface: Looking after a handful of antique coins.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 British pennies were written d (from Latin denarius), so 10d was tenpence.
explanation.definitionFit: To look after or care for something, as a shepherd does a flock, is to tend it.

clue.text: Ruling-for persons about to marry, including Mina ?

indicators.note: the word for persons about to marry holds the name inside it

parts.note: Punch magazine's famous 1845 'Advice to persons about to marry' was simply 'Don't'
taken as written, a woman's name

explanation.surface: A verdict for an engaged couple that brings in a woman called Mina.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue relies on Punch's joke: its whole advice to persons about to marry was 'Don't'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruling, in the sense of governing or prevailing, is a synonym of dominant.

clue.text: Acid is put up £1 by H.P.

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means everything is read upwards

parts.note: the pound sign comes from L, for Latin libra
the figure 1 is one
taken as written, HP

explanation.surface: A chemical is bought for a pound on hire purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: H.P. is hire purchase, British for buying on instalments; 'put up' reads L, ONE and HP from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbolic acid is the common name for this compound.

clue.text: Bookmaker's river or spring

parts.note: a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: A betting shop at the riverside, or by a spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bookmaker' looks like a betting agent but is an author: George Orwell. The Orwell is also a river in Suffolk, England, whose name the writer took.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer of Nineteen Eighty-Four took his pen name from an English river in Suffolk.

clue.text: Animal the god's got in mind

indicators.note: the god's name is put inside the word for mind

parts.note: to mind is to care
Thor is the Norse god of thunder, and the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: Some creature that a deity is thinking about.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy draught horse that pulls a cart is a working farm beast.

clue.text: Part of army centre, say ?

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken, a sound match

parts.note: the core is the centre

explanation.surface: A unit of the army stationed at the middle, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A corps is a large military formation.

clue.text: Interval for some golf, if that's possible

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: A break for a round of golf, provided it can be managed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possible' is part of the surface only, a link phrase with 'if that's'; the answer runs across golF IF THat's.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a fifth is the interval spanning five notes of the scale, such as C up to G.

clue.text: Just about fifty showing natural aptitude

indicators.note: the word for just goes round the numeral

parts.note: just means fair
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Barely fifty, but showing a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural talent or knack is a flair.

clue.text: Can break into capital ? A pretty tale !

indicators.note: the broken letters are set inside the capital's name

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

indicators.note: to break the word can is to rearrange its letters

explanation.surface: A tin bursts into a city, which makes a charming story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a tin or a verb, but it is the anagram fodder; 'break' rearranges it and 'into' sets the result inside the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A love story or adventurous tale of the sort that charms is a romance.

clue.text: The only baggage necessary ?

parts.note: a bag that takes everything you own, so it is the single item of luggage you need

explanation.surface: Travelling light with just one piece of luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: A large travelling bag for carrying sundry belongings is so named because it takes everything.

clue.text: Fibre returned by girl about one

indicators.note: the whole assembly is read backwards
the word for girl goes round the letter for one

parts.note: a lass is a girl
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Some thread sent back by a girl about one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: LASS around I makes LASIS, which 'returned' reads as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong plant fibre from an agave, used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Paltry use made of vicar's suggestion

indicators.note: the words are made into something new, a rearrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A clergyman's proposal gets used in a trivial way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made of' signals rearranging PALTRY USE; 'of' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman's invitation to the congregation to begin praying is a familiar formula from church services.
